subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: When Signal delivers an edit, should OpenClaw supersede the original turn in future context, append both versions as linked turns, or update context without immediately starting another agent run?
rationale: Signal supplies enough metadata to detect edits, but OpenClaw has no established contract for mutating prior inbound turns or deciding whether an edit should retrigger an active conversation.

options.title: Supersede in context
options.body: Keep an auditable edit event but treat the corrected content as authoritative in future context and require an explicit mention before a group edit starts another run.

options.title: Append linked edit
options.body: Keep both versions as distinct turns with structured edit metadata and an `[edited]` presentation marker.

options.title: Context-only correction
options.body: Update future context from the edit but never dispatch an immediate agent response from an edit event.

recommendation.title: Supersede in context
recommendation.body: Keep an auditable edit event but treat the corrected content as authoritative in future context and require an explicit mention before a group edit starts another run.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this contributor to the Signal inbound and dispatch paths where these semantics must be chosen.
